description: Integrate redact-core into the single-file Markdown tracer bullet as the primary structured-identifier engine.
verify: Run the CLI on one Markdown file through redact-core
Observe de-identified Markdown output plus structured-identifier audit output
Observe no false claim of full Safe Harbor coverage yet
notes: Completed in the pivoted iteration by wiring single-file replace/review/dry-run flows through redact-core for built-in structured identifiers, with explicit coverage warnings.

description: Add a Safe Harbor policy mapping layer for redact-core detections.
verify: Map built-in redact-core detections to explicit Safe Harbor policy categories
Express date handling as Safe Harbor policy rather than raw detector output
Differentiate covered identifiers from residual review-required gaps
notes: Completed through bounded policy slices that map structured detections to explicit Safe Harbor-oriented behavior, including year-only date handling, age-over-89 handling, source-aware review summaries, category mapping, and explicit residual-gap reporting.

description: Add configured known-entity replacement for names and known geographic/institutional identifiers that non-AI detection cannot guarantee.
verify: Run configured name/provider/institution/location replacement deterministically
Observe configured replacements distinguished from library detections
Observe residual review signaling for unknown contextual identifiers
notes: Completed through bounded slices covering configured client, provider, institution, and location replacement with review-mode distinction from raw redact-core structured coverage and explicit residual-gap signaling.

description: Provide dry-run and review modes with source-aware replacement summaries.
verify: Run the CLI in dry-run mode without writing final outputs
Observe review summaries showing whether a replacement came from redact-core, config, or custom policy
Observe clear mode-specific CLI behavior
notes: Completed through bounded slices that aligned replace/dry-run/review mode behavior to the pivoted redact-core architecture, surfaced replacement source in summaries, and verified non-writing dry-run/review flows through the public CLI.

description: Process whole directories into de-identified Markdown with include/exclude policy and run summaries.
verify: Run the CLI across a directory of supported inputs
Observe include/exclude filtering
Observe processed/skipped/unsupported/review-sensitive run summary
notes: Completed with directory input support, include/exclude filtering, mirrored Markdown outputs, per-file audit outputs in replace mode, and run-level processed/skipped/unsupported/review-sensitive summaries.

description: Add DOCX to Markdown extraction plus Safe Harbor de-identification.
verify: Extract supported DOCX content to Markdown
Apply the de-identification pipeline end-to-end
Surface unsupported/non-text content explicitly
notes: Completed with DOCX to Markdown extraction through word/document.xml, end-to-end de-identification on extracted text, Markdown output for DOCX inputs, and explicit non-text placeholder surfacing for unsupported drawing/object content.

description: Add custom Safe Harbor gap recognizers and deterministic overlap resolution.
verify: Cover agreed Safe Harbor gaps beyond stock redact-core support
Resolve overlaps predictably among library/config/custom detections
Surface residual review-required cases explicitly
notes: Completed through bounded custom-gap slices covering fax-number and address/sub-state-geography classification layered on top of redact-core, with deterministic overlap suppression and explicit residual-gap reporting in review output.

description: De-identify filenames and generated artifact names.
verify: Output filenames are de-identified deterministically
Review/audit artifacts do not leak raw identifiers in names
Run output explains naming transformations
notes: Completed with deterministic filename and artifact-name de-identification in batch workflows, plus run-summary reporting of renamed outputs.

description: Add text-extractable PDF to Markdown extraction plus Safe Harbor de-identification.
verify: Extract text-extractable PDFs into Markdown
Apply the de-identification pipeline end-to-end
Report non-extractable or low-confidence PDFs explicitly
notes: Completed with text-extractable PDF ingestion via lopdf text extraction into Markdown-like text, end-to-end de-identification on extracted text, and explicit failure for PDFs with no extractable text or invalid/low-confidence extraction.

description: Build a Safe Harbor fixture matrix and regression harness.
verify: Fixture coverage spans supported Safe Harbor categories and formats
Regression tests verify Markdown output plus audit/review behavior
Explicit unsupported and residual-review cases are tested
notes: Completed with a fixture-driven integration harness spanning supported Safe Harbor categories, configured supplementation, DOCX extraction, extractable PDF ingestion, and explicit failure behavior for invalid/non-extractable PDFs.

description: Default clinician directory runs should write Markdown outputs into a predictable redacted folder without reprocessing generated artifacts.
verify: Run the CLI on a directory without explicit output overrides
Observe de-identified Markdown outputs under input/redacted and audit artifacts under input/redacted/.audit
Observe batch summaries remain correct and preexisting generated outputs are not reprocessed
notes: Completed by changing the default batch output root to `input/redacted`, colocating default audit artifacts under `input/redacted/.audit`, and skipping generated output paths during traversal so reruns do not ingest prior artifacts.

description: Unify structured-library detections, policy transforms, and configured replacements behind one provenance-aware finding model.
verify: Run the CLI with a sample that triggers library, policy, and configured replacements together
Observe output, audit artifacts, and review summaries all reflect one stable finding shape with source provenance
Observe current public behavior is preserved while detector provenance becomes consistent across replace, dry-run, and review flows
notes: Completed through two bounded slices: first, explicit provenance labels were added; second, a shared `Finding` model was pushed through policy application, configured replacement, review summarization, and audit generation before rendering final audit records. The public behavior remained stable while detector provenance became an explicit shared abstraction.

description: Add optional local ONNX NER so the tool can run in deterministic-only or ML-assisted mode with explicit model configuration and honest failure surfacing.
verify: Run the CLI in deterministic-only mode and observe current fallback behavior remains intact
Run the CLI with valid local model assets and observe contextual ML detections flow through the public pipeline
Run the CLI with missing or invalid model assets and observe explicit failure or disabled-model reporting rather than silent degradation
notes: Issue #15 now has four bounded slices: optional `[ner]` config plus explicit fallback/failure behavior; a testable recognizer-loading seam for positive ML-style detections; dedicated review-surface reporting for ML-assisted coverage; and an ignored real-local-model acceptance test gated by `TNS_DEID_NER_MODEL_PATH` / `TNS_DEID_NER_TOKENIZER_PATH`. This is enough to keep the repo honest about the remaining asset-dependent gap while preserving a real path to positive local-model verification.

description: Layer psychology-specific contextual coverage on top of the hybrid redaction pipeline for client, provider, school, clinic, guardian, and sub-state location identifiers.
verify: Run the CLI on realistic clinical text containing psychology-specific contextual identifiers
Observe improved redaction coverage in output Markdown and provenance-aware review artifacts
Observe the tool still surfaces residual review-sensitive cases instead of claiming perfect contextual coverage
notes: Completed for the current bounded psychology-specific scope through three deterministic labeled-context slices: (1) client/patient and provider/examiner/clinician/therapist/psychologist fields, (2) family-role fields such as mother/father/parent/guardian/caregiver/spouse/sibling, and (3) institution-style fields such as school/clinic/hospital/institution/employer/workplace/university/college. The product still surfaces residual review-sensitive gaps for broader unlabeled free-text context.

description: Strengthen audit JSON, dry-run output, and review summaries so they clearly surface ML-assisted detections, confidence boundaries, and residual review risk.
verify: Run review mode on a sample with mixed deterministic and ML-assisted detections
Observe clinician-facing summaries distinguish detector provenance and residual review risk clearly
Observe audit artifacts remain machine-readable while carrying enough provenance for downstream inspection
notes: Three bounded issue-17 slices now exist: (1) optional detector confidence is carried through findings, audit JSON, and review summaries when available; (2) audit artifacts include machine-readable review flags for `ml_active`, `has_ml_findings`, and the residual review-gap list; and (3) dry-run/review summaries now include an explicit residual-review-risk summary with open-gap counts, low-confidence ML counts when applicable, and custom contextual finding counts.

description: Deepen extraction reporting so omitted non-text content, weak extraction, and review-sensitive ingestion boundaries are surfaced more clearly to clinicians.
verify: Run the CLI on representative DOCX/PDF inputs with strong, weak, and non-text-heavy extraction outcomes
Observe run summaries and review output distinguish omitted non-text content and weak extraction states explicitly
Observe the text-first Markdown contract remains intact while extraction confidence boundaries are made more honest
notes: Independent hardening slice from GitHub issue #18; can proceed after issue #13 because it does not require the ML boundary to exist first.

description: Extend the end-to-end fixture matrix so it proves deterministic-only and ML-assisted workflows together, including model-misconfiguration and review-risk surfacing.
verify: Run the fixture matrix across representative mixed-document inputs in deterministic-only mode and ML-assisted mode
Observe tests verify output Markdown, audit artifacts, and review summaries as one public workflow contract
Observe the matrix covers unavailable-model or misconfigured-model scenarios with explicit failure or fallback behavior
notes: Final verification slice from GitHub issue #19; depends on the completion of issues #16, #17, and #18 so the matrix reflects the intended product contract.
